description: US-16 Maintain a Customer's Record — Household, address, group, notes and certificate renewal editing on the customer record, with counts, portions and price updating immediately.

userStories.title: updateHousehold use case
userStories.description: As a staff member, I want to add and remove household members, so the record reflects reality as households change. Source: tasks/prd-us-16-maintain-customer-record.md §US-16.1
acceptanceCriteria: updateHousehold(deps, {customerId, members}) replaces the household member set
An empty member list rejects with EmptyHousehold and a future birthdate with BirthDateInFuture, reusing the registration domain rules rather than a second implementation
Derived counts, portions and price are never written
Test asserts a change that alters the counts puts the customer on the cards-due list with reason HOUSEHOLD_CHANGE
Test asserts a change that does not alter the counts (e.g. a spelling fix) does not put the customer on that list
Test asserts no history of the previous composition is kept
Writes an audit entry
Tested against hand-written fakes and a fake clock
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Domain: createHouseholdMembers extracted from createCustomerDetails so an edit is judged by registration's rules. Application: updateHousehold (customer.householdUpdated audit entry); refuses an archived customer (record read-only, FR-8), allows a blocked one. Port + Prisma adapter: updateHousehold(id, members) replaces the member set in one transaction. Tests in src/application/customers/maintain-customer.test.ts drive the real listCardsDueForReissue to prove HOUSEHOLD_CHANGE follows a count change and a spelling fix does not.

userStories.title: updateCustomerDetails and updateNotes use cases
userStories.description: As a staff member, I want to correct a customer's personal data, address and notes. Source: tasks/prd-us-16-maintain-customer-record.md §US-16.2 and §US-16.3
acceptanceCriteria: updateCustomerDetails updates name, date of birth and address with the same validation as registration

The customer's own record and their household-member entry stay consistent when their name or birthdate changes; the mechanism is decided, documented and tested (a single source of truth is preferred)
The customer number is not editable through this use case
updateNotes saves free text as given; empty is allowed, and a maximum length (4000 chars) is enforced with a clear message
Test asserts notes are returned by the counter lookup
Both write audit entries
Tested against hand-written fakes
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Modelling question (PRD §7) settled: the customer's own row and their household-member row are KEPT IN STEP in one write, not unified. A single source of truth needs either dropping the customer from their own household (which breaks EmptyHousehold and contradicts US-16.1) or giving member rows an identity they do not have. So domain replaceHouseholdMember(members, was, becomes) restates the row holding the customer's OLD name and birthdate; CustomerRepository.updateDetails(id, details, household) writes both halves in one transaction. No matching row = household left alone. Domain: createPersonalDetails and createNotes extracted from createCustomerDetails; NOTES_MAX_LENGTH 4000 with the new NotesTooLong error. updateNotes is its own use case (customer.notesUpdated); a test drives the real lookupCustomer to prove the note reaches the counter. Both refuse an archived customer, allow a blocked one. Decision recorded in docs/technical_documentation.md.

userStories.title: changeGroup use case
userStories.description: As a staff member, I want to move a customer between Red and Blue, so the two groups stay roughly balanced. Source: tasks/prd-us-16-maintain-customer-record.md §US-16.4
acceptanceCriteria: changeGroup(deps, {customerId, group}) sets the group and returns the resulting group sizes
Changing to the same group rejects as a no-op
Test asserts a customer moved to Red is servable in a Red week on the same day
The change puts the customer on the cards-due list with reason GROUP_CHANGE, since the card prints the group
Writes an audit entry
Tested against hand-written fakes and a fake clock
Tests pass
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Domain: Card gains a groupAtIssue snapshot — the card prints the group, so a move makes it wrong; without the snapshot there is nothing to notice a move against. That settles US-13's open question. staleCounts.ts is renamed staleCard.ts and staleCardReason takes CardFacts = { counts, group } on both sides, answering AGE_13 | HOUSEHOLD_CHANGE | GROUP_CHANGE; counts answer first, the group only when they agree. Application: changeGroup (customer.groupChanged) returns groupCounts read AFTER the write, refuses a no-op with the new GroupUnchanged error and an archived customer, allows a blocked one. Port + adapter: setGroup(id, group), a single column that deliberately leaves the cards alone. 'In force today' is proved by driving the real lookupCustomer on a RED distribution day (2026-08-05): WRONG_GROUP before, CLEAR_TO_SERVE after, one instant.

userStories.title: Customer record editing on /kunden/[id]
userStories.description: As a staff member, I want one screen where I can see and update everything about a customer. Source: tasks/prd-us-16-maintain-customer-record.md §US-16.5
acceptanceCriteria: Household members can be added and removed inline; counts, portions and price update live
The group control shows both current group sizes next to the choice
Notes are a multi-line field saved explicitly, with an indication that they appear at the counter
The certificate renewal form is embedded and shows the reminder count resetting to 0
Destructive actions (reissue card, block/unblock, archive) are grouped in a clearly separated section, each with its own confirmation
Distribution history is listed newest first with date, showed-up, paid and the price that applied
Each household member shows their current age next to their birthdate
The counter screen (/ausgabe) links to this record and offers 'Sperren' / 'Sperre aufheben' there — carried over from US-08.4, which shipped both controls on the record only
An archived customer's record renders fully read-only
All user-facing strings come from src/i18n/de.ts
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Five forms, five use cases, five audit entries — no merged saveCustomer (PRD §7). HouseholdEditor derives counts/portions/price in the browser from composition/portionsFor/priceFor against the server's today, so the consequence of adding a child shows before the save; priceFor widened to a PriceValues Pick so the client holds only the four per-head numbers. readCustomer gained history (newest first, the record's own priceCents), groupCounts and today; lookupCustomer gained blockReason. Block controls moved up beside the archive ones and are now offered at the counter, which also links to the record (US-08.4 carry-over). Archived renders with zero inputs on the page. The group radios are the one uncontrolled field: React resets a form after its action and a reset restores a radio from its checked ATTRIBUTE, so a controlled one came back on the old group while the sizes beside it showed the new one. Verified in a real browser end to end (live figures, group move + no-op refusal, note reaching /ausgabe, name correction carrying into the customer's own household row only, renewal resetting the count, archived read-only).

userStories.title: E2E: edit a household and see the effects
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a Playwright spec proving record edits propagate to counts, price, group and the counter. Source: tasks/prd-us-16-maintain-customer-record.md §US-16.6
acceptanceCriteria: Spec opens a customer record, adds a child, and asserts counts, portions and price update and that the customer appears on the cards-due list
Spec changes the group and asserts both group sizes update and the counter verdict for today flips accordingly
Spec edits the notes and asserts the text appears on the counter screen for that customer
Spec records a renewed certificate and asserts the reminder count shows 0
npm run test:e2e passes
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: tests/e2e/customer-record.spec.ts, one household (customer number 291 — 281–285 belong to customer-list) seeded BLUE with a lapsed certificate, two reminders and a card printed 1/1 BLUE, pinned to the RED Thursday 08.01.2026. Four edits, each read back off the screen that would betray it: adding a child moves all four derived figures BEFORE the save and then lands on /karten-neuausstellung as HOUSEHOLD_CHANGE; the renewal resets the reminder count to 0; the group move flips the counter from WRONG_GROUP to CLEAR_TO_SERVE on the same morning with both sizes moving as a delta; the note comes back verbatim at /ausgabe. The card is reissued between the household and group edits because stale counts answer the cards-due list first and GROUP_CHANGE would never be visible. Full suite 72 passed, 1 skipped.
